title: We may ask living saints to pray for us, but no one would address them as Rome addresses Mary, Benedict or Nicholas
source_text: XCIII. Certe Sanctos hic nobiscum viventes omnium confessione rogare licet ut Deum pro nobis orent: Nec tamen ferretur qui viro Sancto in terris versanti diceret, ut Mariae Virgini dici solet, Nostra tolle Incommoda, Dona confer caelestia. Nos culpis solutos, Mites fac & castos. Aut ut dicitur S. Benedicto Angustum per iter scandere largiens Dona regna perennia. Sive ut habet hymnus ad Sanctum Nicolaum Aufer mortis dispendia, Confer vitae subsidia: Ut post carnis exilia, Tecum simus in gloria. Quod si quis Apostolos ipsos ea ratione fuisset allocutus, Orationem ejusmodi ut impiam compescuissent, & jussissent ista non a se, sed a Domino peti. An ergo putabimus jam ipsis gratum esse posse, quod olim dum in terris viverent, ut impium & sacrilegum aversati fuissent?
pass_a_gloss: Certainly by everyone's confession it is lawful to ask Saints living here with us that they pray to God for us: Yet he would not be tolerated who would say to a holy man living on earth, as is wont to be said to the Virgin Mary, Take away our Ills, Bestow heavenly gifts. Make us, loosed from faults, Gentle and chaste. Or as is said to Saint Benedict Granting to climb by the narrow way, Give the everlasting kingdoms. Or as the hymn to Saint Nicholas has it Take away the losses of death, Bestow the helps of life: That after the exile of the flesh, We may be with thee in glory. But if anyone had addressed the Apostles themselves in that manner, they would have checked such a Prayer as impious, and ordered that those things be asked not from them, but from the Lord. Shall we then think that this can now be pleasing to them, which formerly while they lived on earth they would have shunned as impious and sacrilegious?
pass_b_english: Everyone admits it is lawful to ask holy people living here with us to pray to God for us. Yet no one would be tolerated who said to a holy man on earth what is commonly said to the Virgin Mary: "Take away our ills, bestow heavenly gifts; make us free of our faults, gentle and chaste." Or what is said to Saint Benedict: "You who grant us to climb the narrow road, give us the everlasting kingdom." Or what the hymn to Saint Nicholas says: "Take away the loss that death brings, bestow the helps of life, so that after the exile of the flesh we may be with you in glory."

If anyone had spoken that way to the apostles themselves, they would have stopped such a prayer as impious and told him to ask for those things from the Lord, not from them. Are we to think, then, that what they would have rejected as impious and sacrilegious while they lived on earth can please them now?

lemmas.gloss: yet he would not be tolerated

choices.term: Angustum per iter scandere largiens Dona regna perennia
choices.english: You who grant us to climb the narrow road, give us the everlasting kingdom
choices.why: Dona is the imperative 'give', parallel to the other petitions, not the noun 'gifts'.
